ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022 and implementing FATF Recommendations; Companies Act 71 of 2008, s 33, read with Regulation 32 (Beneficial Ownership Information); Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024 (beneficial ownership verification and CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register); Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorism and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access: The CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register is filed at incorporation and updated on any change; it is not a public register and access is restricted to competent authorities (CIPC, Financial Intelligence Centre, South African Revenue Service, National Prosecuting Authority, Hawks, the dtic) and other persons acting under lawful authority.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified copy of the passport or national identity document of each foreign director, shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public / competent issuing authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention effective in South Africa on 30 April 1995) or Consular Legalization for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Apostilled certificate of incorporation, memorandum and register of members of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the foreign state's competent authority or Consular Legalization for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled power of attorney authorizing the South African incorporation agent to act on behalf of foreign incorporators
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign director or shareholder before a notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and tax residence certificate for each foreign UBO (for FICA Part C due diligence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign banking institution and foreign tax authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the South African national sanctions list administered by the Financial Intelligence Centre, the OFAC SDN List (required by USD-clearing correspondent banks), UK and EU consolidated sanctions lists (market practice), and the FIC guidance on domestic prominent persons, foreign prominent persons and politically exposed persons. Enhanced due diligence applies to PEP relationships, multi-layered beneficial ownership structures, use of foreign shell entities, and cross-border commodity trading under FICA ss 21A, 21B, 21C, 23A and 42, with risk-based ongoing monitoring commensurate with the Medium_Risk_Enhanced banking AML tier.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC eServices (Companies and Intellectual Property Commission) at https://eservices.cipc.co.za; name reservation on Form CoR 9.1 and incorporation on Form CoR 15.1 with Memorandum of Incorporation and notices of registered office and first directors/auditor.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A proposed name must consist of Latin-alphabet characters and may be in any of the 11 official South African languages without translation; a name derived from a non-Latin script or foreign language must be transliterated into English or Afrikaans and must not be confusingly similar to an existing registered name. The name must satisfy the distinctiveness and non-offensiveness tests of Companies Act s 11 and must end with the suffix '(Pty) Ltd' for a private company.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Building Society, Insurance, Assurance, Trust (restricted under financial-sector statutes; prior regulatory approval required)
National, President, Government, Minister, Commissioner, Ambassador, State (implying official patronage or state connection)
Municipal, Provincial, University, College, School, Chamber of Commerce (reserved to accredited bodies)
International, Group, Holdings, Corporate, Alliance (permitted only upon proof of qualifying structure or ministerial approval)
Offensive, obscene, xenophobic, or inciteful words prohibited by s 11(2)(b)
Names identical or confusingly similar to an existing company name, defensive name, or trademark under the Companies Regulations, 2011
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant should within 10 business days file a fresh CoR 9.1 application containing alternative distinctive names via CIPC eServices. Where rejection is based on similarity or restricted words, the applicant may apply to the Companies Tribunal under s 160 for a determination on the name, or obtain prior ministerial approval from the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition for a sensitive word. The statutory name reservation runs 60 days for a private company (2 months, once extendable) under the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024; previously reserved names continue under the former 6-month transitional rule. Any refusal is a decision subject to administrative review under s 187 read with the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000, with judicial review available in the High Court within 180 days of the refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or registered-agent office is permissible provided that the registered office is a physical address within South Africa (s 23(3) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008) and a post office box is used only as a postal address. Mail-forwarding virtual offices are accepted by CIPC and by commercial banks for KYC and service-of-process purposes, but the company must retain a local agent able to receive process and produce records. For this cross-border battery-metals trading profile, FIC guidance on conduit arrangements and the expectation of local commercial substance require an operational layer: a physical registered office, a contracted South African registered agent, local governance records, and a domestic bank account evidenced by real UBO attestation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15-25% within the first three years: CIPC conducts compliance inspections under s 186 of the Companies Act, and SARS may perform a trade vetting visit upon VAT registration or first export/import declaration; the likelihood increases if the registered office appears to be a passive mail-drop or if bank documentation reflects inconsistencies.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) / foreign competent authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: DIRCO statutory fee ZAR 120 per document, plus courier and translation handling

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended, sections 13 (incorporation), 14 (registration of incorporation), 15 (Memorandum of Incorporation), 19 (legal personality), 23 (registered office), 33 (accounting records), 66 (board of directors) and 84 (audit/accounting officer); Companies Regulations, 2011 (GN R351, 30 April 2011); Companies (Beneficial Ownership Information) Regulations, 2022 as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), South Africa, reporting to the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic); lodgment is effected through the CIPC 'bizfile' online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (CIPC Form CoR 14.1) submitted together with the signed Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI), the Notice of Registered Office and the prescribed Beneficial Ownership Declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum issued or paid-up capital is prescribed by the Companies Act 71 of 2008, and no escrow or capital deposit account is required. The incorporation subscriptions are settled by the consideration recorded in the MOI and the company's securities register; the first directors must ensure that the issued share capital is fully paid for the consideration stated and duly entered in the register of members.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: 1. The registration of the Company under section 14 of the Companies Act, 2008, the adoption of the Memorandum of Incorporation, and the Certificate issued by the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission are ratified. 2. The subscription for the initial ordinary shares is accepted and the shares are allotted and issued fully paid. 3. The registered office notified under section 23 of the Companies Act is confirmed. 4. [DIRECTOR A], [DIRECTOR B] and [DIRECTOR C] are appointed as directors until the next annual general meeting. 5. [NAME] is appointed Managing Director. 6. The directors are authorized to appoint auditors or accounting officers, open bank accounts, register with the South African Revenue Service, and execute all documents giving effect to this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register as a user on the CIPC bizfile e-services portal; complete CIPC Form CoR 9.1 (Name Reservation) listing up to four preferred names in order of priority, each ending with '(Pty) Ltd'; select company type 'Private Company'; pay the statutory name reservation fee of ZAR 50 per name online by credit/debit card; retain the CIPC name reservation reference number for the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Completed CIPC Form CoR 9.1 (Name Reservation)
Certified copy of the identity document or passport of each applicant
Proof of business address of the applicant (if a juristic applicant)
CIPC e-services payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a preferred name is refused for similarity or contravention of section 11(2) of the Companies Act, CIPC automatically proceeds to the next priority name; alternatively, file a fresh name reservation or apply to CIPC for administrative review supported by a letter of consent from the holder of the conflicting name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of the Memorandum of Incorporation and Supporting Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and professional corporate governance counsel (pre-lodgment), with final reception by CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MOI adopting the default provisions of Schedule 1 of the Companies Regulations or, where desired, incorporating prescriptive provisions permitted by section 15(2); complete CIPC Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation) inserting the reserved name, the proposed registered office in the Republic, the date of incorporation, the first directors, and the election regarding an auditor or accounting officer under section 84; complete the Beneficial Ownership Declaration identifying all natural persons holding a beneficial interest in the company; have each incorporator execute the MOI and the Notice of Incorporation; verify all details before lodgment.
required_dossiers: Signed Memorandum of Incorporation
Completed CIPC Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation)
Notice of Registered Office (CIPC Form CoR 15.1)
Beneficial Ownership Declaration
Written consents of the proposed directors to act in that capacity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Engage a registered auditor, chartered accountant, or corporate governance attorney to validate compliance with the Companies Act and the Companies Regulations before submission; correct all omissions in the MOI and CoR 14.1 to avoid CIPC rejection of the lodgment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgment of the Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the CIPC bizfile e-services portal and select 'Register a Company'; choose 'Private Company'; upload the executed MOI, CoR 14.1, and Beneficial Ownership Declaration in PDF form; enter the certified identity particulars of the incorporators and first directors; review the electronic cover page; pay the incorporation fee of ZAR 175 (together with the name reservation, approximately ZAR 225 in total) and submit the application for processing.
required_dossiers: CIPC bizfile electronic CoR 14.1
Uploaded PDF of the executed MOI
Uploaded PDF of the Beneficial Ownership Declaration
Certified copies of the identity documents or passports of incorporators and directors
Proof of payment of the incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues an explanatory query or a refusal under section 14(4) of the Companies Act, rectify the stated defect and resubmit within 10 business days; if a compliance notice is issued, approach CIPC for an extension or appeal the decision to the Companies Tribunal within the prescribed period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval of the application, download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation (CIPC Form CoR 14.2) and the company's registration confirmation from the bizfile portal; verify the company registration number (e.g., 2025/XXXXXX/07), the registered name, and the date of incorporation; keep certified electronic copies for subsequent banking, SARS, and client-facing documentation.
required_dossiers: No external dossiers required; the Certificate of Incorporation is generated by CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a material error (e.g., in the name, date, or registration number), file a rectification application with CIPC supported by an affidavit and the original Notice of Incorporation; CIPC will reissue a corrected certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: South African Revenue Service Tax, VAT, and Customs Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) via the branch office or eFiling portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax through SARS eFiling using the Certificate of Incorporation and appoint a public officer under section 246 of the Tax Administration Act, 2011; apply for VAT registration (mandatory where the value of taxable supplies exceeds or will exceed ZAR 1 million in any 12-month period); apply for the SARS Customs Importer/Exporter code using Form DA185 to enable the cross-border procurement and importation of battery-grade lithium carbonate; provide proof of the registered physical address and the company's banking details in the prescribed SARS format.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.2)
Memorandum of Incorporation
Certified copies of directors' identity documents or passports
Proof of the company's registered physical address (lease or utility account)
Bank confirmation letter obtained under FICA-compliant account-opening procedures
SARS VAT 101 application and SARS Customs Form DA185
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS queries the application, the public officer must attend a SARS branch consultation and present the certificate of incorporation, the MOI, and evidence of the operational address and projected transaction volumes; unresolved queries may be escalated through the SARS service escalation channels or remedied by appointing a registered tax practitioner.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance, Beneficial Ownership, and Operational Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC; Department of Employment and Labour; local municipal authorities; commercial banks
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Beneficial Ownership Information with CIPC within the first compliance cycle and maintain the register of members and the register of beneficial interests at the registered office; hold and minute the first board meeting adopting the pro forma first board resolution; issue share certificates to the subscribers; open a corporate bank account under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act, 2001 (FICA) verification process; register with the Compensation Fund (COIDA) and for UIF if and when the company employs staff; obtain any municipal occupancy and fire certification applicable to the registered premises.
required_dossiers: Beneficial Ownership Declaration filed with CIPC
Minutes of the first board meeting and the first board resolution
Securities register and issued share certificates
Directors' consents and FICA verification documents
COIDA and UIF registration forms (when employees are appointed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the beneficial ownership filing deadline is missed, submit a late filing with CIPC together with an acceptable reason and, where applicable, an application for condonation; failure to comply with a CIPC compliance notice may be cured by full compliance within the extension period granted and, if necessary, by a ruling from the Companies Tribunal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to the trading scope. ISIC 4662 wholesale trade of metals and minerals, including battery-grade lithium carbonate, is not a statutorily licensed or manufacturing activity in South Africa. Sectoral oversight rests with the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic); the International Trade Administration Commission (ITAC) regulates any import/export controls; and SARS Customs issues the mandatory Importer/Exporter Code.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Exempt - no operating or manufacturing license is statutorily required for the wholesale procurement and distribution of battery-grade lithium carbonate. The mandatory operational prerequisites are the SARS Customs Importer/Exporter Code (Form DA185) and, for any warehousing activity, the municipal Certificate of Occupancy and a fire safety clearance issued for the relevant premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE), Environmental Authorizations Branch, applying the Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations, 2014 (GN R982 as amended by GN R326 of 7 April 2017)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no listed activity under Listing Notices 1, 2 or 3 (GN R983, R984 and R985 of 4 December 2014) is triggered by office-based wholesale trading and logistics. However, where the company operates a storage or warehousing facility containing hazardous chemical agents above the thresholds prescribed in the Hazardous Chemical Agents Regulations, 2021, a Basic Assessment may be required under Listing Notice 1, and in limited circumstances a full Scoping/EIA process under Listing Notice 2.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: The pure trading activity generates no process wastewater, VOC or combustion emissions. Any storage of packaged lithium carbonate must comply with the Hazardous Chemical Agents Regulations, 2021 (GN R402 issued under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993) and SANS 10228 (storage and handling of dangerous goods), including impermeable secondary containment to prevent soil and stormwater contamination; all waste disposal must be performed by a DFFE-registered waste service provider in accordance with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act, 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The registered office and any warehouse premises must hold a municipal Certificate of Occupancy issued under the National Building Regulations and Building Standards Act 103 of 1977 confirming structural compliance; a Fire Safety Clearance or Certificate of Fire Compliance must be obtained from the local municipal fire prevention services in terms of the Fire Brigade Services Act, 1987 and applicable by-laws, covering any storage of packaged lithium carbonate; and an Occupational Health and Safety clearance must be registered with the Department of Employment and Labour under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993, including a safety file, risk assessment, and designation of a company safety representative prior to the commencement of operational activities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); eFiling portal at https://www.sarsefiling.co.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A South African Proprietary Limited company (Pty Ltd) is incorporated through the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) and receives an income tax reference number automatically upon registration. VAT registration is mandated under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991 once taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in a 12-month period; voluntary registration is available above ZAR 50,000 in a 12-month period. A foreign entity without South African incorporation must apply through SARS eFiling or a SARS branch using the VAT 101 application, submit its foreign certificate of incorporation or equivalent, appoint or identify a public officer/registered representative, provide a local physical address or place of business, bank confirmation, and supporting resolutions to obtain a VAT vendor number and income tax reference number where South African tax obligations arise.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; resident South African Pty Ltd is taxed on worldwide income; non-resident persons are taxed on South African-source income; no transparent pass-through treatment is available for a Pty Ltd.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a check-the-box system. Available statutory grouping and compliance elections include: VAT group registration under section 50 of the VAT Act for a group of companies; income tax group asset rollover elections under section 45 of the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962; and adjustments or elections required to neutralise domestic and cross-border hybrid mismatch arrangements. No general entity reclassification election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration: ZAR 1,000,000 (R1 million) of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; voluntary registration: ZAR 50,000 of taxable supplies in a 12-month period
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance, or digital stamping regime is presently imposed in South Africa. Vendors must issue valid tax invoices containing the prescribed particulars under section 20(4) of the VAT Act; electronic tax invoices are accepted. SARS eFiling and e@syFile are the official electronic channels for VAT return filing and payment. A vendor exporting goods must retain the prescribed export documentary evidence for SARS audit and refund verification.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of goods by a registered VAT vendor qualifies for zero-rating where the goods are supplied under a sale or export agreement and are physically exported to a destination outside South Africa within 90 days of the time of supply, and the vendor retains proof of export. Offshore services are zero-rated where the services are supplied to a non-resident who is not present in South Africa at the time of supply and the services are not directly connected with immovable property or movable property situated in South Africa, subject to the exclusions in the VAT Act.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) lodged with SARS Customs under the Customs and Excise Act 91 of 1964
Commercial invoice and original VAT tax invoice containing the prescribed particulars under section 20(4) of the VAT Act
Packing list and transport document (Bill of Lading, Airway Bill, or road manifest) evidencing physical movement to a destination outside South Africa
Proof of export, such as a customs-cleared exit report or container movement notification
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or Authorised Dealer confirmation evidencing receipt of the export sale proceeds from the foreign buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may audit any zero-rated export transaction and require full production of the export documentation bundle before accepting or releasing a VAT refund. Failure to substantiate zero-rating results in a retrospective clawback of the VAT previously zero-rated, together with prescribed interest. Penalties include the understatement penalty under section 222 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011, graduated by taxpayer conduct and prejudice, reaching a maximum of 150% of the shortfall for intentional tax evasion. Fraudulent export zero-rating may also lead to criminal prosecution for false declarations under the VAT Act and the Customs and Excise Act, with imprisonment up to 10 years and additional customs penalties or forfeiture.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), exercising delegated powers under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act 9 of 1933), the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961, with enforcement coordination through the Financial Intelligence Centre Act, 2001 (FICA) framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa maintains a partially convertible exchange-control regime: ZAR is fully transferable on current-account transactions, while capital-account flows are regulated. Import payments for battery-grade lithium carbonate are freely dispensable through an Authorised Dealer upon presentation of the SARS customs entry (SAD500), commercial invoice, transport document and an import-of-goods purpose code; no prior FinSurv approval applies to genuine trade settlements. Inward foreign equity investment is freely permitted subject to mandatory electronic reporting by the Authorised Dealer to FinSurv (the modern successor to legacy Form N reporting), and carries no minimum capital threshold for a (Pty) Ltd. Profit remittances to foreign shareholders are permissible on current account through an Authorised Dealer after a lawful dividend declaration and settlement of the statutory 20% dividends tax (double-tax-agreement relief may apply). Capital repatriations (share redemption, capital reduction) require proof of the original inward-investment reference, and shareholder-loan repayments require prior Exchange Control Regulation 10 approval for the underlying borrowing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (Companies Act 71 of 2008, s. 33)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of the company's date of incorporation or registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a CIPC penalty fee and the company is flagged non-compliant, preventing certificates of good standing; failure to file the Annual Return for two consecutive years permits CIPC compulsory deregistration (strike-off) under s. 82(3) and s. 83 of the Companies Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership (UBO) confirmation and BO register filing (s. 56 as amended by General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering) Amendment Act 22 of 2022)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: UBO declaration filed with, and confirmed as accurate in, the CIPC Annual Return; separate BO updates due within 30 days of any share transfer or change of beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance results in a CIPC compliance notice, suspension of the company's compliance/good standing status, restriction on share transfer registrations, and an administrative offence for directors under the General Laws Amendment Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) for the completed tax year, together with provisional tax declarations (IRP6) and top-up payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual return due on or before the last day of the 12th month following the financial year end; first provisional payment due 6 months after year end, second provisional payment by year end, top-up payment within 6 months after year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: SARS administrative non-compliance penalties per Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 (up to ZAR 16,000 per month for repeat non-submitters or 5% of outstanding tax), 3.5%-plus interest on underpayments, and criminal liability for directors for persistent non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Interim reconciliation due 31 October (March-August tax period); annual reconciliation due 31 May (March-February tax year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed administrative penalties for late submission under the Tax Administration Act; SARS may audit the employer's register and PAYE liability and recover interest on late remittances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act (COIDA) - Return of Earnings (W.As. 8)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Employment and Labour - Compensation Fund
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 1 March covering the preceding assessment year (1 March to 28/29 February)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file permits the Compensation Fund to make an estimated assessment; the employer remains liable for compensation claims without cover and the non-submission is an offence under COIDA subject to a fine.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) and applicable audit or independent review report (s. 30 and s. 90, Companies Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and the company records; AFS are not filed with CIPC for private (Pty) Ltd companies unless the company is public, state-owned, or expressly required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AFS must be prepared within 6 months after the financial year end; audit or independent review report signed before presentation to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may receive a CIPC compliance notice; continued default supports an application for director delinquency or personal liability civil action by shareholders; the company loses its compliance status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A South African private (Pty) Ltd company is required to appoint an auditor and undergo a statutory audit if: (a) its Public Interest Score (PIS), as computed under s. 59(1) and Companies Regulation 26, equals or exceeds 500; (b) a person holds a beneficial interest in the company's securities; (c) the MOI requires an audit; or (d) the company is subject to an audit under another law. A company with PIS of 130 or more but less than 500 must instead undergo an independent review by a registered accounting practitioner, unless the shareholders unanimously elect an audit. A company with PIS below 130 is exempt from both audit and independent review unless the MOI or shareholders determine otherwise. PIS is calculated as 1 point per employee, 1 point per R1 million of third-party liabilities, 1 point per shareholder, and 1 point per beneficial owner.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (for public, state-owned, listed and certain large companies) or IFRS for SMEs; South African Statements of Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (SA GAAP) aligned with IFRS continue to be available to private companies. The adopted framework must be applied consistently and stated in the AFS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must keep a beneficial ownership register, file it with CIPC within 30 days of preparation or amendment, and confirm its continued accuracy in each Annual Return. Every share transfer resulting in a change of beneficial ownership requires a fresh BO declaration to CIPC within 30 days. BO filings are a prerequisite for maintaining CIPC compliance status and issuing certificates of good standing; directors failing to lodge or keep accurate BO records commit an offence under the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering) Amendment Act 22 of 2022 read with the Companies Act.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - 800 per annum (approx. ZAR 4,500 - 14,500) for registered office, company secretarial, annual return preparation and compliance monitoring by a CIPC-registered agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Independent review (PIS 130-499): USD 900 - 2,500; full statutory audit (PIS 500 or more): USD 4,500 - 14,000, dependent on transaction volume, foreign counterparty documentation and inventory of lithium carbonate purchase contracts

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023 (s5(1) Income Tax Act 58 of 1962); the Small Business Corporation rate of 21% applies only where the Pty Ltd is a qualifying SBC with all individual shareholders and annual turnover below ZAR 20 million, not relevant to a battery-metals procurement vehicle.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Research and development deduction under s11D at 150%; renewable energy allowance under s12B with accelerated wear-and-tear up to 125% of cost; manufacturing plant allowance under s12C at 40% first year and 20% per annum thereafter; industrial policy project incentive under s12I; foreign tax credits under s6quat for lithium-carbonate supplier-country withholding; assessed losses are carried forward with no fixed 5-year limit in South African law, subject to the same-trade requirement in s20(1) and the s20A change-of-ownership ring-fence.
